references.name: David Ricardo
references.desc:
Architect of classical economics; his
    victory over Malthus buried effective demand
    for a century

references.name: Alfred Marshall
references.desc:
Keynes's teacher at Cambridge; embodiment
    of the classical tradition being
    overthrown

references.name:
A.C. Pigou, Theory of
    Unemployment
references.desc:
Most precise formulation of classical
    employment theory; dismantled in Ch. 19
    appendix

references.name: Thomas Robert Malthus
references.desc:
Proto-Keynesian who argued excess saving
    can check growth; defeated by Ricardo

references.name: Jean-Baptiste Say
references.desc:
Author of "Say's Law" that supply creates
    its own demand — the axiom Keynes
    rejects

references.name: R.F. Kahn
references.desc:
Invented the employment multiplier concept
    in 1931; Keynes's closest intellectual
    collaborator

references.name:
Irving Fisher, Theory of
    Interest
Friedrich Hayek
references.desc:
Austrian school; identifies marginal
    efficiency with interest rate, getting
    conclusions "exactly the wrong way
    round"

references.name: Knut Wicksell
references.desc:
"Natural" or "neutral" rate of interest
    concept; influential on Keynes's earlier
    Treatise on Money

references.name:
Silvio Gesell, The Natural Economic
    Order
references.desc:
"Unduly neglected prophet" of stamped
    money; half-right theory of interest as
    monetary phenomenon

references.name:
Bernard Mandeville, Fable of the
    Bees
references.desc:
1723 allegory proving luxury spending
    sustains prosperity; convicted as public
    nuisance

references.name:
J.A. Hobson & A.F. Mummery,
    Physiology of Industry
Piero Sraffa
references.desc:
First to analyze commodity "own-rates" of
    interest (1932); influenced Ch. 17

references.name: Karl Marx
references.desc:
Coined "classical economists"; effective
    demand lived in his "underworld" after
    Ricardo's triumph

references.name: D.H. Robertson
references.desc:
Cambridge colleague; alternative savings-
    investment definitions; today's income =
    yesterday's output

references.name: R.G. Hawtrey
references.desc:
Critic emphasizing "liquid capital" and
    unsold stocks; read entire proof-sheets

references.name: Joan Robinson
references.desc:
Read entire proof-sheets; member of
    Keynes's inner circle at Cambridge

references.name: John Locke
references.desc:
First abstract expression of money-interest
    relationship; "parent of twin quantity
    theories"

references.name: Adam Smith
references.desc:
Favored moderate usury laws; aware that
    savings may be absorbed by debt rather than
    investment

references.name: Major C.H. Douglas
references.desc:
A+B theorem contains "much mere
    mystification" but valid destructive criticism
    of orthodoxy
